newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Soccer-Thailand, Singapore on course for Tiger Cup semis.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Thailand, Singapore on course for Tiger Cup semis.

text.p: Tiger Cup favourites Thailand continued their confident march toward the semifinals with a 6-0 demolition of Brunei on Friday, while Singapore beat the little-fancied Philippines 3-0.
Singapore's win took them to the top of Group B in the Southeast Asian tournament but Thailand have a game in hand.

The shine was taken off Thailand's emphatic win by news that playmaker Surrachai Jautturapatarapong is likely to miss the remaining preliminary matches, and possibly the rest of the tournament, with an ankle injury.

"We should know tomorrow but we have to consider that we may lose him for the whole of the Tiger Cup," team coach Thavatchai Sajakul said after Surrachai was carried off the pitch in agony 26 minutes into the game.
Worrawot Srimaka did a fine job as Surachai's replacement, scoring twice. Striker Natipong Sri-Tongin also grabbed two goals, while Phithaya Santawong and Kiatasuk Senamuang scored one each.
Singapore's side were knocked out of their stride by some ferocious tackling from the Philippines.
But Fandi Ahmad scored two goals for them in the first half before defender Lim Tong Hai added a third in the 73rd minute.
Singapore's wastefulness in front of goal will worry coach Barry Whitbread as he prepares for their crucial final qualifying match against Thailand on Tuesday.
